paraphrase: Having bowed to Nārāyaṇa, full of all qualities and free of defects, the meaning of the sūtras is stated. In the Dvāpara age, when knowledge had everywhere become confused, the Lord Nārāyaṇa, entreated by Brahmā, Rudra, Indra and others, descended as Vyāsa; he divided the lost Veda and composed the Brahmasūtras to settle its meaning (quoting the Skanda).
speaker: Madhva

paraphrase: (Quoting the Bhāgavata-tantra:) Those entitled (adhikārin) are of three grades, low, middle and highest. By birth, the best among humans are the lowest grade, sages and gandharvas the middle, gods the highest; by qualities, one devoted to Viṣṇu who merely studies is the lowest, one with calm and the other virtues the middle, and the highest is one who, knowing everything from Brahmā to a blade of grass to be worthless and impermanent, has become dispassionate, takes Viṣṇu's feet as his sole refuge and has renounced all works.
speaker: Madhva

paraphrase: (Quoting the Vyoma-saṃhitā:) Even the outcaste (antyaja) who are devotees are entitled to the knowledge of the Name; women, śūdras and degraded brāhmaṇas are entitled to the knowledge of the Tantra (Pañcarātra) in part, as taught by others, not from the text itself; the three twice-born classes who have right devotion to Hari are entitled to what the Veda teaches; and superior women such as Urvaśī, Yamī and Śacī are said to be entitled to the Vedic as well.
speaker: Madhva

paraphrase: Since without Nārāyaṇa's grace there is no liberation, and without knowledge there is no abundant grace, therefore inquiry into Brahman is to be undertaken.

paraphrase: (Quoting the Nāradīya:) Grace won by ritual action is the lowest, grace won by hearing and the like is middling, and grace from fullness of knowledge is the highest; from the lowest comes heaven, from the middling worlds such as Janaloka, and the highest alone gives liberation. Hearing, reflection, meditation and devotion are the principal means to the fullness of knowledge; without them no one has ever gained knowledge.

paraphrase: The word 'Brahman' refers to Viṣṇu alone. (Quoting the Bhāllaveya śruti:) all names enter him, and him the wise call the supreme Viṣṇu; (quoting the Harivaṃśa:) in the Veda, the Rāmāyaṇa, the Purāṇas and the Bhārata, at the beginning, the end and the middle, Viṣṇu is sung everywhere.
speaker: Madhva

paraphrase: (Quoting the Varāha:) Hari says he will create delusion to delude people and bids Rudra cause deluding treatises to be made, showing untrue doctrines and concealing him; (quoting the Brahmavaivarta:) Brahmā says that neither he nor Śiva nor the others have more than a fraction of Acyuta's power, and that Acyuta plays with them as a child with toys.
speaker: Madhva

paraphrase: Brahman is that from which come the creation, maintenance, dissolution, control, knowledge, ignorance, bondage and release (of the world) (quoting the Skanda: 'Hari, the sole sovereign, is the Person from whom come origination, maintenance, dissolution, control, knowledge, covering, bondage and release').

paraphrase: One returns from the other world with a remainder of karma; and (quoting a smṛti) since from the fourteenth year a person, by rule, performs actions that are causes of at least ten further bodies, how could liberation ever come from exhausting karma (by experiencing it)?

paraphrase: The liberated have true desires only in the sense that their desires are not separate from (accord with) the Supreme Lord's; (quoting the Brāhma:) the power belongs to the Supreme — for the liberated only desiring in accordance with his desire is ordained.

paraphrase: At the time of departure the tip of the heart lights up; the knower goes out by the door it illumines, by the power of knowledge and by remembering the path that belongs to it — (quoting the Adhyātma) by the grace of Hari abiding in the heart, departure through the crown opening (brahmarandhra) happens for one who worships him; of the hundred and one channels of the heart, one goes to the crown, and going up by it one reaches immortality.

paraphrase: Those who have reached (the world of) Brahmā go on to the Supreme together with Brahmā, its presiding lord, when that effect-world passes away at the great dissolution (citing the Sauparṇa śruti and a smṛti: 'all of them, with Brahmā, at the dissolution, enter the supreme abode').

paraphrase: Those who do not rely on a (limited) symbol are led to the Supreme. (Quoting the Gāruḍa:) those whose vision of God is confined to their own body 'rely on a symbol'; the gods, a hundred sages, a hundred kings, a hundred gandharvas and the like are entitled to see him as all-pervading, others not; one who strives for a vision he is unfit for falls even from what he had. Those who see Brahman in their own body reach the world of Brahmā and, with Brahmā, the supreme abode at the dissolution.
speaker: Madhva

paraphrase: (Quoting the Gāruḍa:) Having worshipped Hari as the Self, some are released here and do not depart; some abide here, some in the atmosphere, heaven, Mahar, Jana, Tapas or Satya worlds; those of great knowledge go to the Milk Ocean, and there too come nearer by degree of knowledge. Their liberation is sālokya, sārūpya, sāmīpya and yoga (sāyujya). Kings, human and divine gandharvas, ancestors, gods by birth and by merit, the presiding deities of the principles, Prajāpati, Rudra and Brahmā are each a hundredfold above the one before in eternal bliss, enjoyment, knowledge and lordship, and are honoured by those below; Brahmā is honoured by all. Those in union (sāyujya) enter the Supreme Self and come out again, and enjoy enjoyments of consciousness (and some others).
speaker: Madhva
